t: Christianity began among the followers of Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish teacher crucified in Jerusalem around 30 CE, whom they proclaimed risen from the dead, the Messiah and the Son of God.

Spread by apostles such as Paul across the Roman Empire, it survived persecution, became the empire’s religion under Constantine and Theodosius in the 4th century and shaped the civilisation of Europe.

Divided between East and West in 1054 and again by the Reformation in the 16th century, it spread worldwide with missions and empires and is today the largest religion, with about 2.3 billion followers.
dyk: The custom of counting years from the birth of Christ, “anno Domini”, was devised by the monk Dionysius Exiguus in 525; he probably placed the birth a few years too late, which is why historians date it to about 6–4 BCE.
ev: Jesus of Nazareth is crucified in Jerusalem under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate
The apostle Paul writes his letters to the churches, the earliest Christian texts
Constantine and Licinius grant Christians freedom of worship, the so-called Edict of Milan
The Council of Nicaea, called by Constantine, defines the faith in the Nicene Creed
Theodosius I makes Nicene Christianity the religion of the Roman Empire
The Great Schism divides the Latin West from the Greek East
Martin Luther’s Ninety-five Theses begin the Protestant Reformation
The Second Vatican Council reforms the Catholic Church

f.origin: Roman Judea and Galilee, about 30 CE
f.founder: Jesus of Nazareth, whom Christians call the Christ; spread by his apostles, among them Peter and Paul
f.scriptures: The Bible: the Old Testament (the Hebrew Bible, with further books in some churches) and the New Testament
f.followers: About 2.3 billion (2020): the largest religion in the world, with the most followers now in sub-Saharan Africa
